decisions.text: behaviour: server/middleware/rate-limit.js was saved in Windows-1252 (one em dash in the plan 528 comment), and the edit tools could not change it, so I rewrote it as UTF-8 with the same text plus the new exports. Reverse: git checkout the old file and re-add the plan 543 exports in Windows-1252.

behaviour: the honeypot passes through any website value that is not a non-empty string (a number or an object) and does not treat it as a bot. Reverse: in server/middleware/honeypot.js, answer 201 for any truthy website value.
behaviour: added the ADR 0030 entry to docs/workflow-kit/manifest.json (this file is always allowed by scope-check) so kit-manifest-check passes. Reverse: remove that entry.

behaviour: the main folder's map title already read 'APPROVED by Dandan 2026-11-10 (map + contracts)…'. I replaced it with the plan's exact title line, so the extra 'Arch: approve arch change INV-1 given 2026-11-10' note on that line is gone — reverse: restore the old first line from the main folder's copy.
behaviour: the brain index has no list of links, so I added the pointer as a row in its 'When to read what' table — reverse: delete that row.

behaviour: the dry run prints the 9-digit phoneKey in each collision line, because the plan specifies that line format. Printing the key rather than the full phone is what keeps phones out of the output. Reverse: print only the ids and names.
behaviour: the e2e spec deletes the client again in its cleanup, so the QA client ends in Trash, not purged. Reverse: purge it from Trash in cleanup.

behaviour: the local migration ran with NODE_PATH pointing at the main folder's server/node_modules (the worktree has no top-level mongodb) and a copy of the main folder's gitignored server/.env, which I left in the worktree — reverse: delete server/.env

behaviour: for the [ui] run I temporarily pointed environment.local.ts at port 3100 and added a throwaway Playwright config; both are removed and nothing of them is committed. The gate's default config uses :4200 and :3000, which are the main folder's servers, so those would run the old backend — reverse: n/a
seen: the migration scripts require 'mongodb' through server/migrations/tools/_connect.js:12, which pnpm does not resolve in a worktree — a worktree run needs NODE_PATH

behaviour: staff reads of the Trash list now get the same trimmed fields as their other reads (GET /:type/trash in server/routes/generic.js). Without it, staff would have seen the notes, email and consent of trashed clients — reverse: remove the projection option from that find().

behaviour: the migration 0011 dry-run summary uses the Functional Requirements format 'clients: <n>, to patch: <m>, phoneKey collisions: <k>'. The Done-when line gives a shorter form without 'to patch' — reverse: drop the to-patch part in printPlan().

behaviour: migration 0011 leaves updatedAt unchanged on the clients it fills, and its collision list skips clients that have mergedInto set — reverse: add updatedAt to the $set in write(), and remove the mergedInto skip in collisions().

seen: server/routes/generic.js:151 trashOwnerFilter lets staff restore-all or empty Trash for docs whose createdBy is their own id. Once plan 545 stores a staff actor as createdBy on clients, staff could restore or purge those clients even though clients are owner-only.

seen: server/scripts/db-backup.js:31 and server/migrations/tools/_connect.js require('mongodb'), which is not a direct dependency in server/package.json. In this worktree the migration tools only ran with NODE_PATH pointing at mongoose's node_modules.

behaviour: the CSV export button fetches the file with the session token as a blob and saves it, because a plain link cannot send the Bearer header — reverse: change exportAiCsv and downloadAiUsageCsv in platform-admin.service.ts to open a URL

behaviour: the per-business totals use a metered row's businessId as the key, with `__platform__` shown by its raw key when the business has no name — reverse: map `__platform__` to a label in aggregateAiUsage

behaviour: I did not re-read the Google pricing page (no network lookup in this run) and used the plan's prices unchanged, including the Human-chosen gemini-3.8-flash 0.375 / 1.875 — reverse: edit server/constants/ai-prices.js
behaviour: bulk DELETE of clients is a hard delete in the code today, not soft, so I left it alone (the live key goes with the doc) — reverse: add a $unset of liveKey if bulk delete becomes soft
behaviour: a PUT that keeps the phone only fills a missing liveKey when no other live client has that key, so an old twin stays editable — reverse: always set liveKey and answer 409 on E11000
behaviour: trash.service.ts reads the 409 messageKey itself, because readServerRefusal only handles 400s — reverse: widen readServerRefusal (outside this plan's scope) and call it instead
behaviour: owner POST of a client keeps the sent source and defaults it to 'manual' when none is sent — reverse: force 'manual'
seen: server/test/clients.test.js:~213 — the existing server-field and restore tests had to change: liveKey became a server field, POST now sets firstSeenAt and counters, and restore now sets liveKey

behaviour: used a throwaway server on port 3101, ng serve on 4201 and an /api proxy through wt.localhost, plus a temp playwright config and a copy of server/.env, because the dev servers on 3000/4200 run the main checkout. I removed the temp files and stopped the servers afterwards — reverse: nothing to undo.

seen: e2e/helpers/qa-session.ts:~20 — Node fetch to `localhost:3000` gets ECONNRESET on this machine, because the API listens on IPv4 only and `localhost` resolves to ::1 first. `E2E_API_URL=http://127.0.0.1:3000` works around it.

seen: playwright.config.ts — with the default config the spec tests whatever is on :4200/:3000. In this setup that is the main checkout, so the gate's rerun of the spec needs servers started from this branch. Otherwise it fails with the toast missing.

behaviour: the unique indexes `frontdesk_slug_unique` and `frontdesk_business_unique` are partial on `slug` being a string, so raw fixture docs without a slug (server/test/admin-business.test.js inserts two docs per business into every collection) cannot break startup or the cleanup tests — reverse: drop `partialFilterExpression` in server/db.js and give that test's fixtures a
behaviour: `requestKinds` uses `z.partialRecord` because zod 4 `z.record(enum)` requires all four kinds — reverse: switch to `z.record` and fill all four kinds in every profile
behaviour: the PUT response also drops `whatsapp.phoneNumberId`, not only reads — reverse: remove the delete line in the PUT handler of generic.js
behaviour: `qualify` skips the opening-hours check only when `ctx.kind` is `'event'`; with no `ctx.kind` it checks the hours — reverse: require `ctx.kind` in the check

behaviour: the client mirror `permission.service.ts` does not mirror `OWNER_ONLY_TYPES`, so the UI can still show create for staff on frontDeskProfiles while the server refuses — reverse: add a type check in `can()`

behaviour: the publicToken unique indexes on requests and bookings are partial (publicToken is a string), so a raw fixture doc without a token cannot break startup, as with the profile slug index — reverse: drop the partialFilterExpression in server/db.js

behaviour: a request with an unfit verdict but no missing answer is stored `qualified`, per the plan's rule that only a missing required answer gives needs_info — reverse: map verdict unfit to another status in runQualify in server/routes/requests.js
behaviour: the client data services return error codes and log them, with no toast, per the plan's 'codes only' note — reverse: add UserMsgService calls in the run() helper

behaviour: I did not tick the 15 unticked items left in the plan's list around lines 127–166. They read as spec items, not sub-tasks, and the plan file was not changed this round — reverse: tick them in the plan file.

behaviour: decisionLog is registered with backup:false although the plan says backup:true, because server/test/collections.test.js (outside scope) requires userData:true for any backup entry — reverse: set backup:true once that rule is relaxed
behaviour: approve builds and validates the event or booking before the claim, so a 400 never touches the request; only an insert failure reverts the claim — reverse: move the build after the claim
behaviour: a client with more than 3 kinds after approve keeps the last 3 (the schema maximum) — reverse: change the slice in requests.js approve

behaviour: RequestDataService.approve reloads the menu events store when it is loaded, because MenuEventDataService has no public add method and is outside scope — reverse: add a method there and call it
